headline: Chinese start-up DexForce says training humanoid robots in simulated worlds is a cheaper route to useful robots than collecting real-world data from human workers.
score_reason: Interesting industry method but one company's claim, with no results shown in the text we could read.
importance_line: Robot makers and the factories, offices and homes that want them could benefit if simulation works, but it is one start-up's bet, based on its chief executive's word.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by Oman Observer, that DexForce, a humanoid-robot start-up based in Shenzhen, trains its robots on synthetic data from virtual environments instead of recording human workers, to cut costs. Chief executive Jia Kui told Reuters that collecting real-world data to reach what he calls 'physical artificial general intelligence' would need 10 trillion samples, which he called fundamentally inefficient.
